I found a **current blue Staffordshire Bull Terrier listing around Inverness**, but I’d treat marketplace adverts cautiously rather than assuming the seller is a responsible breeder. One listing currently advertises blue Staffy puppies, with males and females, vet checks, first vaccinations, worm/flea treatment and microchipping claimed by the seller. [Staffie-Owners.co.uk](https://www.staffie-owners.co.uk/staffies-for-sale/inverness?colour=blue&sex=male&utm_source=chatgpt.com) 

For a more reliable starting point, the **Royal Kennel Club's Find a Puppy** service lets you filter Staffordshire Bull Terriers by location and, importantly, whether both parents have been health tested. [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/find-a-puppy/?ActiveCertifiedBreeder=False&Breeds=Staffordshire+Bull+Terrier&Distance=15&FemaleDogs=False&GeneralRescueClubs=False&HealthTested=False&MaleDogs=False&SearchRescueClubs=False&SortNearest=False&TotalResults=0&utm_source=chatgpt.com) 

[royalkennelclub.com](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/find-a-puppy/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

### What I'd ask the breeder

Before paying a deposit, ask:

- **Can I see the puppy with its mother, at your home?** Don't agree to a car-park handover or meeting somewhere unrelated to where the litter was raised.
- **What health tests have both parents had?** For Staffies, specifically ask for evidence of:

 - HC-HSF4 hereditary cataracts DNA testing
- L-2-HGA DNA testing
- eye testing
- elbow testing
 These are among the health screening measures recommended by the Royal Kennel Club for the breed. [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/breeds-a-to-z/breeds/terrier/staffordshire-bull-terrier/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- **Can I see the actual certificates/results, rather than just "health tested"?**
- **What are the parents' temperaments like?** Ideally meet both if possible.
- **What's the puppy's coefficient of inbreeding (COI)?** Ask for the parents' KC details so you can check it yourself.
- **Has the litter had a veterinary examination?**
- **What vaccinations, worming and flea treatment has the puppy received?**
- **Is the puppy microchipped and registered to the correct details?**
- **Will I receive the KC registration/pedigree paperwork, contract and health records?**
- **How are the puppies being socialised?** Ask about household noises, handling, children, other dogs, grooming, car travel, etc.
- **How many litters does the breeder produce each year?** If they're producing three or more litters in a 12-month period in Scotland, licensing requirements apply.
- **Will you take the dog back or help rehome it if I can no longer keep it?** A good breeder should care about the dog's lifetime welfare.

### One thing about "blue" Staffies

**Blue is an accepted Staffordshire Bull Terrier colour**, so there's nothing inherently wrong with wanting a blue puppy. However, the Royal Kennel Club explicitly says colour should not take priority over health and temperament. [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/breeds-a-to-z/breeds/terrier/staffordshire-bull-terrier/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) 

I'd also be wary of anyone charging a large premium *just because* the puppy is blue, or advertising terms such as "rare blue", "XXL", "micro", or "exotic"—those aren't reasons to pay more for a Staffy.

If you give me your **maximum driving distance from Inverness (e.g. 50, 100 or 200 miles)**, I can look for currently advertised blue Staffy litters and narrow them down to breeders where there is evidence of the parents' health testing.
